query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Crew service is arguably the strongest driver of SIA ratings/recommendations, and a 4-way qualitative categorisation (warm/professional/robotic/rude) gives a genuine grouping axis beyond the raw Staff Service score. However groundedness is a real problem: in the seats-dreadful review (sample 2) the source text mentions nothing about crew, yet the value is 'rude_dismissive' — an invented negative. The near-even warm(3207)/rude(3073) split hints at systematic over-assignment of 'rude_dismissive' to negative reviews regardless of crew mention.

per_column.name: food_quality_issue
per_column.rationale: Categorises food into actionable failure modes (taste, quantity, special-meal) rather than just echoing the numeric Food & Beverages score, so it adds leverage for identifying improvement levers. Samples are well grounded: praise mapped to 'praised_or_acceptable', and reviews silent on food correctly returned 'Unknown' rather than fabricating a category.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_issue
per_column.rationale: Partially overlaps the existing numeric Seat Comfort column, but the issue-type breakdown (narrow/outdated/broken) is more actionable for targeting fixes, so it is not trivially redundant. Grounded in samples: 'seat far too narrow' → narrow_or_insufficient_legroom, comfortable seats → comfortable_no_issue, silence handled sensibly.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: Disruption handling is a plausible major driver of non-recommendation, so isolating it is a useful new axis. All sample reviews lack disruptions and are correctly marked 'not_applicable' — appropriate silent handling; no evidence of fabrication.

per_column.name: customer_service_resolution_quality
per_column.rationale: Captures post-flight/complaint resolution, distinct from inflight service, giving a separate improvement dimension relevant to detractors. Samples that never contacted service are correctly 'not_contacted' rather than invented outcomes.

per_column.name: ground_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Check-in/boarding/lounge is a genuine axis absent from the original numeric ratings, useful for locating friction outside the cabin. Samples with no ground-service mention are marked 'no_issue', a defensible default though slightly optimistic; no clear contradictions observed.

per_column.name: ife_quality
per_column.rationale: Adds an issue-type view over the existing Inflight Entertainment numeric column. Groundedness is mixed: sample 2's 'sound...dreadful' fits a technical fault more than 'limited_or_outdated', and sample 4's review never mentions IFE yet was tagged 'excellent_or_adequate' — an over-confident positive where the text is silent. Positive/silent cases are otherwise handled reasonably.

per_column.name: cabin_class_experience_gap
per_column.rationale: The gap between class paid for and experience delivered is a valuable lens for premium-cabin improvement. It is fairly inferential, though: it requires combining Class with sentiment, and sample 2 (a very negative economy review) mapped to 'meets_class_expectations' is debatable. No outright invented facts, but values lean interpretive.

per_column.name: service_decline_perception
per_column.rationale: A bare boolean flag that is narrower than the qualitative columns and risks being close to a sentiment marker, so leverage is modest, though 'perceived decline vs past SIA' is a distinct brand-narrative angle. Samples with no temporal comparison correctly return 'false' rather than asserting a decline.

per_column.name: service_consistency_across_legs
per_column.rationale: Useful for pinpointing where multi-leg journeys break down and separating one-off from systemic issues. Single-route reviews are correctly labelled 'single_leg' in every sample, showing appropriate restraint rather than fabricating leg-level variation.

judge.rationale: The added columns form a coherent decomposition of free-text reviews into actionable service dimensions (crew, food, seat, IFE, ground, disruption, complaint resolution, class-gap, consistency, decline) that map directly onto levers SIA could pull to lift ratings and recommendation, and they enable grouping/comparison of non-recommending reviews by failure type — genuinely useful for this query, with only mild redundancy against the existing numeric sub-scores. Groundedness is generally solid, and silent rows are appropriately handled with 'Unknown'/'not_applicable' rather than fabrication. The main weaknesses are crew_service_quality (a clear 'rude_dismissive' assignment on a review that never mentions crew, plus a suspiciously high rude share suggesting systematic over-negativity) and ife_quality (asserting IFE quality where the text is silent), which pull the table-level groundedness down.
